figures.caption: Figure 2: Integration of the HDE Module into the Ads Ranking Model. Left: The viewer SID (𝑐1, . . . , 𝑐𝐾 ) is encoded once per request by the HDE Module (Section 4.4), producing euser — a dense vector constant across all 𝐿 positions in the sequence. Right: Per-event features at position 𝑡 are encoded through standard embedding tables. Fusion (Eq. 10): At every position 𝑡 , the user embedding is summed with the event-level embeddings before a shared LayerNorm, yielding input tokens {h𝑡 }. The resulting sequence is processed by the Transformer stack and scored by the CTR head. All HDE embedding tables are trained end-to-end under the CTR objective.

Table 2: RQ-FSQ on two heterogeneous pre-trained embedding sources. 𝚫AUC is measured against the no-SID baseline — the production ranking model with no member SID input. Storage is the per-user serialization footprint relative to the raw float32 embedding of the same source. RQ-FSQ matches the dense embedding’s AUC on both sources at 30–280× smaller storage.

Table 1: Cross-domain user SID results (RQ-KMeans quantization, 𝐾=3 codes per source). ΔAUC relative to no-SID baseline. Upper block: single-source SIDs ordered by behavioral activity richness. Lower block: multi-source combinations. The RQ-FSQ comparison against the same sources appears in Table 2.
